idiom_name: module method with a case/hash lookup over duck-typed DAOs (Sequel.connect or establish_connection selects the store)
implementation_notes: Ruby DAOs are plain objects answering the same messages, so the DAO Factory is a module method with a case/when or a frozen hash of lambdas returning the right class initialized with the configured handle; there are no interfaces to declare and no abstract factory to subclass. The store-selection half is the database library's: Sequel.connect("postgres://...") resolves the adapter from the URL scheme (or takes adapter: explicitly) and ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection does the same from config, so the hand-written factory only maps a store key to your DAO classes. Keep one initializer that builds the single handle and one module that hands out DAOs bound to it.
code_sketch:
module UserDaoFactory
  DAOS = {
    "postgres" => ->(db) { PgUserDao.new(db) },
    "sqlite"   => ->(db) { SqliteUserDao.new(db) },
  }.freeze

  def self.for(store, db)
    DAOS.fetch(store).call(db)        # KeyError names the bad store key
  end
end

DB = Sequel.connect(ENV.fetch("DATABASE_URL"))   # adapter picked by URL scheme
users = UserDaoFactory.for(store, DB)
pitfalls: Sequel.connect without a block retains the database in Sequel::DATABASES, so calling it per request leaks connections; connect once in an initializer and pass the handle down.
Duck typing hides interface drift: a DAO missing a method fails only when called (NoMethodError), so back the family with shared conformance tests or a shared module.
Sequel and ActiveRecord pool connections per process; a factory whose DAOs each connect create competing pools and transaction boundaries that do not line up.
